title: Harcourt Trophies Grade 2 Teacher Guide — Suggested Lesson Planner + Cross-Curricular Centers

structure.description: A 5-day at-a-glance spread organized as columns (Day 1-5) against rows (skill strands). The left sidebar lists all skill strands; each day column fills in the specific activity for that strand. Everything centers on ONE reading selection for the entire week.
structure.colorCoding: Each day gets a distinct color (red, orange, green, blue, pink/purple). Skill strand headers use consistent color-coded badges.

oralLanguage.dailyPattern: Alternates between stories and poems across the 5 days. Day 5 compares story to main selection.

wordWork.dailyPattern: Day 1: introduce phonograms + pretest. Day 2: review + build words + introduce vocab. Day 3: state generalization. Day 4: expand to syllables + review. Day 5: post-test + writing application.

reading.dailyPattern: Day 1: decodable readers. Day 2: read main selection + comprehension. Day 3: reread for fluency + connected nonfiction. Day 4: comprehension test + locate information. Day 5: fluency reread + self-selected reading.

languageArts.dailyPattern: Writer's Craft appears all 5 days (Developing Ideas and Topics). Grammar: introduce Day 1, review Days 2-5. Daily Language Practice: error correction exercise every day. Writing prompts get progressively freer (Day 1: favorite topics → Day 5: self-selected topic).

dailyRoutines.description: Fixed daily routines that happen regardless of the story. Provides predictable structure.

progressionPattern.description: Clear introduce → practice → generalize → apply → assess arc across the 5 days. Nothing is one-shot. Every skill gets revisited at least 3 times in different contexts before the post-test.

days.day2: Build + read main selection (apply in context)
days.day5: Post-test + self-selected reading + writing application (demonstrate mastery)

crossCurricularCenters.description: A two-page spread of 5 learning centers, each connected to the story theme (chameleons). Every center targets a DIFFERENT subject while reinforcing the reading selection. Each includes: activity description, time estimate, materials list, and a photo/illustration of the expected output.

centers.name: Science Center
centers.description: Build a mock chameleon habitat using natural materials (shoe box diorama with real leaves, twigs, sand, construction paper). Discuss blending/camouflage and survival.
centers.storyConnection: extends the chameleon theme into real science

centers.name: Literacy Center
centers.description: Use chameleon-shaped acetate cutouts with phonograms -ide and -id. Children place consonant/blend cards in front to build and read words. Record words in Word Building journals.
centers.storyConnection: chameleon-themed manipulatives reinforce the week's phonograms

centers.name: Computer Center
centers.description: Write compare/contrast sentences: how the story chameleon is different from a real chameleon. Use spell-check. Practices writing + technology.
centers.storyConnection: fiction vs. nonfiction analysis of the chameleon

centers.name: Social Studies Center
centers.description: Draw a map of an imaginary zoo like the one in the story, using letter and number grids. Practices map skills + spatial reasoning.
centers.storyConnection: the zoo setting from the story becomes the map subject

centers.name: Drama Center
centers.activity: A Day in the Life of a Chameleon
centers.description: Act out chameleon behaviors (catching flies with party blowouts as tongues, changing colors). Engage in dialogue and dramatic play.
centers.subjectConnection: drama (role play, creative expression, oral language)
centers.storyConnection: embody the chameleon character from the story

eachCenterIncludes: colored header bar with subject icon
designPattern.iconStrip: Row of 5 subject icons across the top (Science microscope, Letter & Word ABC, Technology globe, Social Studies earth, Drama masks) — visual wayfinding for which center is which

overallLayout.spacing: dense but organized — color coding prevents overwhelm
overallLayout.visualHierarchy: color-coded columns dominate, skill strand sidebar provides navigation
overallLayout.flowDirection: left-right across days, top-down within each day

difficulty.complexity: multi-skill (entire week across all subject strands)

theming.visualStyle: color-coded information design (teacher reference, not student-facing)
theming.colorPalette: full-color (red, orange, green, blue, purple day columns)

printFormat.orientation: landscape spread (2 portrait pages side by side)
printFormat.colorRequirement: needs color — color coding is structural, not decorative

weekAtAGlance.description: One two-page spread shows the ENTIRE week's instruction for one reading selection. Parent/teacher can see Monday-Friday at a glance without flipping pages. This is the single most powerful planning feature — it eliminates 'what do I do today?' and shows how each day builds on the last.
weekAtAGlance.value: reduces daily planning overhead to near-zero for the parent

spiralReview.description: Skills introduced early in the week get reviewed and deepened across subsequent days. Spelling starts with a pretest (Day 1), builds words (Day 2), generalizes the pattern (Day 3), reviews (Day 4), and ends with a post-test + writing application (Day 5). Nothing is taught once and dropped.
spiralReview.value: spaced repetition built into the weekly structure

storyAsHub.description: Everything radiates from ONE reading selection. Phonics, spelling, vocabulary, comprehension, writing, grammar — all connect back to the same story. The cross-curricular centers extend the story theme into science, social studies, drama, and technology. The story IS the curriculum for the week.
storyAsHub.value: coherence — the child isn't context-switching between unrelated topics all day

centersWithMaterialsLists.description: Every cross-curricular center includes: a clear activity description, estimated time, and a MATERIALS box listing exactly what the parent needs. This is the same 'respect the parent's planning time' pattern Carolyng identified in the school-home connections and unit study drops.
centersWithMaterialsLists.value: parent can prepare materials in advance — no mid-lesson scrambling

testedSkillMarkers.description: Skills that will appear on the end-of-selection test are marked with a bold T throughout the planner. Parent knows exactly which activities are 'must-do' versus 'nice-to-do.'
testedSkillMarkers.value: prioritization — if time is short, focus on T-marked activities

gaps.name: weekly-lesson-planner
gaps.description: A week-at-a-glance planner that maps daily activities across skill strands for one reading selection or unit topic. 5 day columns, skill strand rows, color-coded. Shows the introduce→practice→generalize→apply→assess arc. This is a PARENT-FACING planning tool, not a student worksheet.

gaps.name: cross-curricular-center-cards
gaps.description: Individual activity cards for learning centers, each themed around the week's story/topic but targeting different subjects (science, literacy, social studies, drama, technology). Each card includes: activity description, time estimate, materials list, example photo/illustration. Could be generated alongside a weekly plan.

notes: This is the teacher/parent planning layer of the Trophies system — the orchestration that ties the practice worksheets and assessments together into a coherent weekly flow. Carolyng explicitly loved: (1) the weekly breakdown/layout, (2) the focus on the week as a unit, and (3) the cross-curricular centers. Combined with her earlier two drops (practice pages + assessments), she's now shown us the FULL three-layer architecture of a published curriculum: lesson planner (orchestration) → practice book (daily skill-building) → assessment (verification). This is the most significant product architecture signal yet.
